planting.note: Plant bare-root or container trees in late winter to early spring; Gordon needs only about 400 chill hours and is fully self-fruitful.

directions: Plant bare-root or container trees in late winter to early spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun. Gordon arose as a chance seedling discovered on a Whittier, California property and was patented in 1976 for its unusually reliable fruiting in mild-winter climates. It needs only about 400 chill hours and is fully self-fruitful, so a single tree can be planted where cross-pollination options are limited. Fruit ripens late August into September, with firm, crisp, aqueous white flesh under yellow-green skin washed and striped with dark red, good for fresh eating and cooking alike. In Gulf Coast plantings it pairs well with Anna or Dorsett Golden as an extended-season companion.

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container trees in late winter to early spring; needs only about 100 chill hours, among the lowest of any named apple.

directions: Plant bare-root or container trees in late winter to early spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun. Pettingill was found as a chance seedling near Long Beach, California, and introduced in 1949; its chill requirement of roughly 100 hours makes it one of the lowest-chill named apples available, suited to areas where even Anna and Dorsett Golden struggle to accumulate enough winter cold. Fruit ripens late in the season, from late September into mid-October, later than most other low-chill selections, giving Gulf Coast growers a fall harvest option. The large red-over-green apples are crisp and juicy with well-balanced sugar and acid.

common_name: Mollie's Delicious Apple (Low-Chill Sweet Red Apple)

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container trees in late winter to early spring; not self-fruitful, so plant with Fuji, Granny Smith, or Beverly Hills for pollination.

directions: Plant bare-root or container trees in late winter to early spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun. Bred at the Rutgers New Jersey Agricultural Experiment Station from a multi-way cross involving Golden Delicious parentage and released in 1966, Mollie's Delicious carries a Red Delicious-style name and blush but is genetically unrelated to that variety. It needs around 400 chill hours or less, well within Gulf Coast winters, and ripens mid-to-late August with a sweet, aromatic flavor and red-blushed yellow skin. Because it is not self-fruitful, plant it alongside Fuji, Granny Smith, or Beverly Hills for reliable cross-pollination and fruit set.
sources: Rutgers New Jersey Agricultural Experiment Station

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container trees in late winter to early spring; needs about 425 chill hours; watch for scab and fire blight in humid conditions.

directions: Plant bare-root or container trees in late winter to early spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun. Michal was developed by breeder Chanan Oppenheimer in Israel and is conditionally recommended by University of Florida trials as a mid-season companion to earlier Gulf South standards like Anna and Ein Shemer. It requires roughly 425 chill hours and ripens later in summer than Anna, extending the harvest window into the humid, disease-pressured part of the Gulf Coast season. Fruit is medium-sized, round to slightly oblate, and notably crisp compared to many other low-chill selections. Growers should watch closely for scab and fire blight given its later ripening into wetter conditions.
sources: UF/IFAS Extension — Low-Chill Apple Cultivars for North Florida (EDIS HS764/MG368)
